transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-07-13
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Priya Nair (Redwood AE); Jonas Miller (Redwood SE); Lena Ortiz (Redwood Solutions Eng); Dr. Maya Rao (CedarPath Head of Security); Evan Holt (Platform Eng); Sofia Kim (Compliance)

Summary: 
Quick review of BYOK/HSM handover requirements, encryption at rest and in-transit expectations, audit log retention and RBAC/SSO integration. Goal: align on POC scope, SLA items, and artifacts to exchange for legal/security review.

Topics: SOC 2/ISO artifacts, KMS/BYOK mechanism, HSM on-prem connector, data residency, audit logs schema, RBAC/SSO, incident response hooks.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Priya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call — we have Maya, Evan, Sofia on CedarPath side?
[00:05] Dr. Maya: Yep hi, this is Maya. Thanks for setting up.
[00:07] Evan: Evan here.
[00:09] Sofia: Sofia — hey all.
[00:11] Priya: Great. Jonas from Redwood is with me. Jonas, want to intro?
[00:15] Jonas (Redwood SE): Yep, hi all. I'm Jonas, I'm going to run through the technical handover bits — BYOK flows, H S M connector options, and the audit/logging expectations.
[00:22] Dr. Maya: Perfect, high level for us — CedarPath is running regulated genomics workloads, so data residency and key custody are non-negotiable. We need to know how we can bring our keys, what custody models you support, and how audit logs reflect key usage.
[00:38] Priya: Understood. To set expectations: Redwood supports hosted with customer-managed keys via BYOK through KMS integrations, dedicated pools with tenant-level isolation, and an on-prem H S M connector for private deployments. Today we'll walk through the tradeoffs and the artifacts we can hand over.
[00:52] Evan: Quick question — for hosted with BYOK, where are the keys stored? In our cloud KMS or in your H S M?
[00:58] Jonas: With BYOK the recommended pattern is customer KMS as the root of trust. Redwood performs envelope encryption — we never persist the unwrapped key. The DEKs are encrypted with your KMS-wrapped key. For HSMs we support wrapping in external H S M and can do a transport key via an approved handshake.
[01:19] Sofia: When you say "we never persist the unwrapped key" — can you show where that is documented? We need that for SOC 2/ISO evidence.
[01:27] Priya: Yes, we'll share the BYOK runbook and the integration playbook after the call — secure link. It'll include sequence diagrams, API calls, and where the key material is transient.
[01:35] Dr. Maya: And audit logs — we need cryptographic evidence of key usage per request. That includes key id, operation (wrap/unwrap), timestamp, requester identity and origin IP.
[01:46] Jonas: Right — Redwood's audit schema includes key_id, operation, requestor_id (token or SAML subject), model_id, and action latency. We can extend to include origin ip and zone if you require; we'll need to map that to your retention window.
[01:59] Priya: What's your retention window requirement?
[02:01] Dr. Maya: Minimum 7 years for certain datasets, but for keys usage logs we typically require 3 years.
[02:07] Evan: That's a lot. Are there additional costs for long retention?
[02:10] Priya: There's an add-on for extended log retention in Redwood Console. We'll share pricing in the follow-up. It's configurable per customer.
[02:18] Jonas: Also note, for on-prem H S M connector we can keep log output local to your SIEM; Redwood will write a signed event stream you can pull — so retention and residency live with you.
[02:29] Sofia: Good. How about SSO/SAML integration — mapping of roles to RBAC? We need fine-grained control so only select service accounts can call decrypt/wrap operations.
[02:39] Jonas: We support OIDC/SAML SSO with SCIM for groups. You can map groups to Redwood roles. The crypto-sensitive operations are gated behind an elevated role which can be limited to specific service principals.
[02:49] Dr. Maya: Are the admin operations audited separately?
[02:52] Jonas: Yes, admin actions (key rotation, rewrap, role changes) are separately flagged in the audit stream with a higher severity and tie back to the user id and IP.
[02:59] Evan: For POC we want to test rotation impact on latency — how quickly does rewrap propagate and do in-flight requests failover gracefully?
[03:07] Jonas: Good question. For typical envelope rotation the runtime supports a dual-key window — new tokens use the new DEK while existing KV cache entries continue using the old one until flushed. In practice, rewrap is near-instant for new requests, and in-flight requests may hit a brief cache miss but we have automatic fallback to fetch and rewrap. We'll simulate real traffic during POC.
[03:26] Dr. Maya: You mentioned KV cache, sometimes we see it written as K V cash in some notes — just flagging transcription stuff, haha. But operationally, we want guarantees that cached tokens are invalidated after rotation.
[03:37] Jonas: Yes we'll include the cache invalidation timing and the config knobs — TTLs, explicit flush endpoints — in the runbook.
[03:44] Sofia: On the legal/compliance side, we need chain of custody for keys during any support-assisted key import. If Redwood personnel ever interact with the keys, what controls exist?
[03:56] Priya: Support-assisted imports are governed by JIT access: access is ephemeral, logged, and requires SSO MFA, a support-runbook request, and customer approval. We can also limit support roles to read-only for logs and deny any unwrapping operations.
[04:12] Dr. Maya: Is there an option for escrow — in case of emergency?
[04:15] Priya: We support an escrow pattern using an encrypted key envelope stored in a customer-controlled vault; the unwrapping requires multiple approvers from your side. We have templates for key escrow policy.
[04:26] Evan: Network constraints — we have strict egress rules; we want the H S M connector to operate over private peering.
[04:33] Jonas: On-prem connector supports VPC peering and private link. For hosted you'll set up a KMS endpoint in your cloud, and Redwood will connect outbound to your KMS endpoint over TLS; we can also do an on-prem proxy for air-gapped environments.
[04:45] Dr. Maya: Can you outline the fallback behavior if your region is unavailable? Data residency is strict, but we need SLA for availability.
[04:53] Priya: For strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private deployments. Hosted can fallback to nearby region but that's not acceptable for residency constraints. For Dedicated you can configure cross-region fallbacks with explicit approval. We'll include recommended deployment topologies in the POC doc.
[05:07] Sofia: For SOC 2 evidence, we also need to see configuration drift controls, attestations, and the last audit date.
[05:14] Priya: We'll share SOC 2 Type II report and ISO 27001 certificate.via the secure artifact link. Also include recent pen-test exec summary.
[05:24] Evan: About encryption in transit — do you support mutual TLS to the H S M connector?
[05:28] Jonas: Yes mutual TLS for H S M connections is supported. We also support client certificate rotation and short-lived certs via your PKI.
[05:36] Dr. Maya: For the POC, can Redwood run a small synthetic workload that hits 16k seq models so we can measure token latency under KV cache and without cache?
[05:45] Jonas: Absolutely. We'll run three scenarios: cold start (no cache), warmed KV cache, and during key rotation. We'll capture 95th/99th p99 latencies and token-level cost.
[05:56] Priya: OK, quick recap and next steps. I'll send the BYOK/H S M runbook and SOC 2/ISO artifacts by Friday. Jonas will prepare the POC test plan and latency/cost estimate. Evan, you'll share network topology and the list of audit fields you require.
[06:12] Evan: Yep, I can get that to you by 2026-07-21.
[06:15] Sofia: We'll expect the secure artifact link with documents — please mark it as access restricted.
[06:19] Priya: Yes, we'll use a short-lived signed link and request SSO access.
[06:23] Dr. Maya: One last quick thing — incident response playbook: do you expose webhook hooks when a key is used outside expected patterns?
[06:30] Jonas: We can emit anomaly alerts to your SIEM — either via streaming signed events or webhook to an ingestion endpoint. We'll include recommended alert thresholds.
[06:37] Dr. Maya: Great. That should do it, thanks.
[06:40] Priya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and schedule the POC kick-off for the week of 2026-07-27.
[06:47] Jonas: I'll email the test plan and initial scripts.
[06:50] Evan: Thanks all.
[06:52] Sofia: Bye.

Meeting end: 15:55 UTC

- BYOK/HSM Runbook (will be shared as secure link)
